findings.reason: A bounded red test showed an over-limit diff could leave a proposed record before the caller received file_too_large. Diff validation now precedes all private object/record writes, and the regression asserts both store directories remain empty.

A bounded red test showed create cleanup failure after a successful exclusive link was reported as zero-effect conflict even though the target existed. The mutation bit is now set immediately after replace/link, so later cleanup or fsync failures report file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=applied and preserve the writer claim.

The final suite exposed a test assertion that replayed an unchanged record and expected a quota error at exact capacity. The implementation correctly allows projected size == max_bytes; the regression now uses a larger recovery record and verifies the rejection boundary.

New-diff review found that secure-runtime admission checked descriptor-relative os.rename while record and target replacement called os.replace, which is not advertised in os.supports_dir_fd on the current runtime. A simulated ENOSYS replacement failed during prepared persistence before the fix; both call sites now use the checked descriptor-relative os.rename primitive and the regression passes.

A bounded red test showed that a candidate-object read failure after the durable prepared transition escaped as file_invalid_record, which suggested a zero-effect retry and released the recovery claim. The apply path now preserves the writer claim and reports file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=none when preparation cannot be completed; the target remains unchanged and the prepared record stays available for inspection.

Fresh-context review found that the new recovery handler called the fallible claim-preservation path before committing the no-release decision. If the store was unavailable, the raw store error could escape and finally could release the prepared lock after recovery. The handler now sets preserve_claim before attempting preservation, tolerates a preservation failure, and still returns file_recovery_required with effect_disposition=none; a mocked-outage regression covers the path.

New-diff review found that a string containing an unpaired surrogate escaped from candidate UTF-8 encoding as UnicodeEncodeError instead of the declared file-change validation boundary. A red regression reproduced the raw exception with the target and private store still empty; encoding errors now become FileChangeError before any proposal persistence.

why: PC-FILE-CHANGE-1 requires a real non-Git or dirty-Git fixture to persist a closed proposal and before image, bind trusted confirmation, safely apply, independently read back and persist a truthful receipt.
not_doing: No expanded undo package, restart reconciliation, tool-contract registration, CLI/Session/UI/model wiring, default write entry, shared queue/CHANGELOG edit or public action.
diff_walk: pocketchat/file_change_store.py: private content-addressed objects, closed JSON records, quota checks, duplicate-member rejection and identity-bound cooperative writer claims.

pocketchat/file_changes.py: closed proposal/confirmation/apply state machine, bounded paths/content/diff, before identity+hash binding, no-follow target traversal, atomic replace/create, independent readback and recovery-required receipt failures.
pocketchat/tools.py: one unregistered proposal helper that persists pending evidence only and exposes no immediate overwrite.

tests: real temporary filesystem and dirty-Git fixtures cover create/replace, stale/revoked grants, path replacement, secure-runtime refusal, quota, prepare/receipt failures, writer collision and effect disposition.
bilingual docs: record the internal store and safety boundary without claiming a command surface, undo path or release.
static_checks: The immutable proposal digest covers schema, id, owner, origin, policy, path, operation, after object and before image.
Target mutation requires exact confirmation, unchanged current policy/write grant, matching target identity/hash and the live writer claim.
Every successful replace/link is classified before later cleanup/fsync/readback work; durable receipt failure preserves prepared state and writer claim.
No default model or user write path is added by this checkpoint.
After prepared is durable, candidate-object read or verification failure preserves the writer claim and cannot be classified as a zero-effect retry.
Candidate-read recovery sets the no-release decision before fallible claim preservation; preservation failure cannot degrade the result to a raw store exception.
Candidate UTF-8 encoding failures are contained as FileChangeError before private proposal persistence and cannot leak UnicodeEncodeError.
